units.title: Back corridor: found a culprit (maybe)
units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Update on the back corridor the dogs won't walk after 2am. Tonight at 02:15 I got the maintenance ladder and took the cover off the air vent halfway along. There was a dead mouse in the duct, been there a while by the smell. Bagged it, sprayed the vent, put the cover back. Biscuit the lurcher still sat down at the corner on the 3am round, but Pip and Juno walked it. I'll take two out of three.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: There you go, Jo. Nine times out of ten it's something you can smell that you can't. Dogs have noses like a weigh station scanner. Biscuit's probably just decided that corner is his now, he'll come round. I'll be through your town Thursday night if you want a coffee from the truck stop, the good one, not the machine.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Thursday sounds good, Merle, park round the back by the exercise yard and the dogs will tell me you've arrived. Biscuit had his breakfast and a long sniff of the vent this morning and seemed satisfied, or at least less worried. I'm calling it the mouse. Mostly.

units.title: Dead air, night six
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Same number, same minute, sixth night running: 03:17, it rings, I pick up, script says 'thank you for calling, how can I help', and there's nothing. Not breathing, not a line hum, just very clean silence for exactly forty seconds and then it drops. Team lead says log it and move on. I've logged it six times. I'm starting to say goodnight to it before it hangs up.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: (sorry, between calls) also the hold music has been changed to a pan pipe version of something that was already bad, and a man rang at 03:40 to ask if his electricity bill could be 'read out slowly' because he couldn't sleep. I did. He thanked me. Best call of the night honestly

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Forty seconds of clean silence at the same minute each night sounds to me like a machine with good manners. Somewhere along our coast a system is trying to reach a number it has been told to reach, and finding only you. I hope you go on saying goodnight to it. It costs nothing, and the night is long out here either way.

units.title: Corridor lights, again, and a deadline
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: status report from the lab: 1. chapter three is a crime scene. 2. fourth energy drink. 3. at 01:35 the motion lights at the far end of the corridor came on, section by section, towards the lab door, like someone walking at normal speed. stopped at the last panel before my door. nobody came in. 4. facilities ticket submitted, again. 5. back to chapter three, which is scarier

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Rin. You bought four energy drinks from me at eleven. The corridor lights are not your biggest problem. Come by at four, the steamed buns are fresh then.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: taro you are not allowed to count my drinks, that's a violation of shopkeeper confidentiality. ok it was four. ok i'll come for a bun. if the corridor lights follow me down the stairs i'm moving into your shop

units.title: Housekeeping: week two notes
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: a few reminders as the threads get busier. Lamp Hours is for company on the night shift, not campfire stories. Share what happened to you, as it happened, with your own time zone if you're abroad, so people don't think it's three in the morning everywhere at once. Be kind to sceptics and to the people they reply to. And drink some water, all of you. Ines

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Seconding the water, and adding: if you notice yourself writing 'and then I looked again and it was gone', note the time and how long you'd been awake. Not because you're making it up, but because that detail is the most useful one for anyone trying to help you work out what happened. It usually matters more than the thing itself.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: thanks Ines love I've stuck a bottle of water in my cleaning trolley at the depot like you said last week and I do feel better for it and the drivers laugh at me but they've started bringing their own so I've started something

units.title: Gate 7 monitor: IT's verdict
units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Log, 00:40 local. IT came out this afternoon about camera 14, the one that shows a figure at the edge of the lot, south fence, by the reefer stacks. Their verdict: ghosting artefact on the encoder, an old frame burned in and bleeding through in low light. They showed me the same thing on another channel. Fair enough. Patrolled south fence at 00:40 anyway. Nil found. Still shows on 14 at 00:55.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: That's a very plausible verdict. Encoder ghosting and burned-in frames were common on older systems, and low light makes them worse because the compression has less real detail to replace the old frame with. One test: does the figure ever move? A burned-in ghost won't. If it's always in exactly the same pixels, that settles it.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Checked against last week's stills. Same pixels, within a few. Doesn't move during a session. Sometimes absent for whole shifts. IT's answer stands as far as I can test it. Logged: 'artefact suspected, camera due for replacement'. Patrolled, nil found.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Our old system at the retail park did the same, a burned-in shopping trolley that sat in the corner of camera 3 for a year after the real one was gone. Control used to call it the ghost trolley. Your south fence one sounds more annoying though, because it's a person-shape. Hope they swap the camera soon.

units.title: The van, week two
units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: First tray of rye in at 02:40, smell of caraway everywhere, and the white van is back across the street with its engine running. Fourth night this week. Lights off, windows fogged, exhaust ticking out into the cold. Nobody gets out, nobody comes in for bread, which frankly is the strangest part. Who idles outside a bakery at three and doesn't want a roll?

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Plate number? If it's a port contractor they sometimes sleep in the cab between early slots. I can check it against the gate list if you get it. Also, thanks for the rolls last night. Shift improved by 40 percent.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Windows too fogged to see in and the plate's caked in harbour muck, but I'll try when I do the bins at four. Only 40 percent? I'll put more butter in tomorrow's batch. Rolls at four as usual, gate seven, and I'll do an extra for the van in case it ever wants one.

units.title: Intercom: three nights of quiet
units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Quick one from break. Since maintenance swapped the call button in bay four, the intercom has not said a single name it shouldn't. Three nights of quiet. Turns out the old button had a cracked housing and the damp was making it call on its own, and the system read out whoever was last assigned to that bed in the old record. Dmitra, you were right. Back to it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: I'm glad it's quiet. It's horrible, a machine saying the name of someone who's gone home, even if you know why. Damp in a call button is so common that the sleep clinic had the same fault in a bathroom pull-cord last winter. No names, just a lot of alarms. Sleep well when you get there.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: I'm so glad for you. I keep hoping ours is a button too. The front door intercom here still buzzes at 03:10 most nights and Mrs A. still says 'that's for me' every time, very calmly, and goes back to sleep. Our maintenance man is booked for next week. I'll ask him to look at the housing first.

units.title: A small question for anyone awake
units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: What do you read when you can't sleep and don't want to be clever? I've been working through a shelf of old sea stories from the shop, the kind where every chapter ends with someone lighting a pipe. At three in the morning they are better company than anything recent. I'd be glad of suggestions, as long as nobody dies in the first chapter.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: the back of a crisp packet in the B corridor vending machine queue, mate, which I can recite. also there's a bookcase in the relatives' room on the fourth floor with eleven copies of the same detective novel, someone's been donating it for years. the murderer is the vicar. sorry. you said nobody dies in chapter one and he doesn't, it's chapter four

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Seed catalogues. My father read them every winter by the stove. Nothing happens in them except things growing. End of shift now, on the bus, snow on the headframe and the sun not up for three hours yet. Read your sea stories. Pipes are fine.

units.title: Forecourt diary
units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: 00:30. Man buys one egg. Just one. Asks if I can put it in a bag. I put it in a bag. 01:10. Student buys four energy drinks and a bun, says nothing about corridor lights, I say nothing about drinks. 02:00. Taxi driver asleep at pump four. I let him be. 03:40. Woman asks if we sell umbrellas. We do. It isn't raining. She buys two.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: the bun was excellent, thank you, and i appreciated the silence on the drinks. the corridor lights didn't come on at all last night, which was somehow worse, because i kept looking up at the door every five minutes waiting for them. chapter three is now merely bad

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Merely bad is good for a chapter three. Mine was a fried noodle display that fell over. Also the egg man came back at four for a second egg. He is building something. I respect it.

units.title: The 03:10 buzz, still
units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: It's 03:10 here and the front door intercom has just buzzed, one long buzz. I've been to the door: frost on the step, nobody, no footprints in it. Mrs A. is awake in room six and says 'that's for me' with a little smile, like someone has rung to say they're on their way. I sit with her a while and she settles. I'm writing this down so I'm not only writing it in the night book.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Liv, two things that might be worth checking. A regular time suggests a timer or a temperature effect, and 03:10 is about when outdoor temperature bottoms out and condensation peaks in a door unit. And residents with dementia often attach meaning to a regular sound. Neither makes it less moving that she smiles. Ask your electrician to look for moisture in the panel.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: She texted me this from the night desk, I'm at the bottom of the shaft. It was minus nine on the gauge at the lamp room when we came up for break. Cold enough to make anything buzz. Dmitra's probably right. Doesn't make it easier for Liv at three in the morning.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Thank you, Dmitra. I'll ask about moisture. I think you are probably right about the cold. I'm sorry for the long post. It's just that she is so sure, and so happy about it, and I'm the only one awake to see it. Back to the rounds now.

units.title: Found the pinging scanner
units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Mystery solved at 02:05. The scanner that's been pinging from empty aisle 41 for three nights was under a pallet of dog food in the bottom bay, wedged sideways, battery at 3 percent, still trying to connect to the network every ninety seconds. Some legend dropped it on Monday and didn't report it. Supervisor's response: 'well that's one less ghost'. Target was 140 picks an hour. I did 112. Good night all.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Ha, our yard got a call on the radio about that pinging last night, Control wanted to know if it was coming from our side of the fence. I'll tell him it was dog food. He'll be disappointed. He'd started a theory.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: My favourite kind of ending. Something regular, something that sounds deliberate, and underneath it a machine doing exactly what it was built to do with nobody listening. Well done for crawling under the pallet.

units.title: Car park nights: a quiet one
units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Quiet one tonight. Control's dozing on the radio, I can hear him breathing between calls. The van from last week hasn't come back, I've been checking the far bays every lap anyway. Kettle's on in the hut, I've got the 3am lap in a minute and then the long stretch till the cleaners come at five. Anyway what's everyone on tonight, anyone got a decent break. hang on, the camera's

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: on a decent break? mate I'm on my fourth trolley run of the hour and the lift on B corridor has started making a noise like a sad goose. I'll answer your question properly when you answer what the camera's doing. probably a fox. it's always a fox

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Dev? you've left us on a cliffhanger mate. our yard's quiet, our floodlights are on, nobody's reported anything over the fence. I'm off at half four. If you're out on a lap just say so when you're back

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Dev love it's gone five and you've not come back and I know you're probably fine and filling in a form somewhere but I've just got off the depot bus and read this and I'll feel better when you post

units.title: Fare that wasn't in the back
units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: ok strange one picked up a bloke at the hospital rank at about 03:05 local, quiet, long coat, gave an address out by the ring road. halfway there he asks me to stop at the edge of the big lit car park by the furniture warehouse, says he'll walk the last bit. I pull over, turn round for the fare, back seat's empty, door shut, no money, nothing. anyway I might have dozed at the lights before that, I'd been on since ten

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: You've just described a runner. They do it from our rank once a month, usually after A&E: sit quiet, ask for an odd stop, slip out while you're reaching for the meter. You were on since ten. That's five hours. Go and get a coffee and don't pick up any more long coats. Back to it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Microsleep at the lights, then a quiet passenger who took his chance: that's my guess, and I mean it kindly. After five hours on nights you can lose two or three seconds without knowing it, and a car door closes quietly if someone wants it to. Please be careful driving home. That's the bit that worries me.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: yeah fair I hear you both. ward9 knows the rank better than me. only thing is I didn't hear the door and I always hear the door, it squeaks, been meaning to oil it for a year. anyway I've stopped for a coffee at the all-night place by the station and I'm going home after this one, promise

units.title: Wind on the gallery
units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: It's a little after half past ten here, and the wind has come round to the north and found every gap in the lantern room. I've been up to clean salt off the panes, which you do by feel at night because the beam blinds you if you look along it. Below, the sea is doing what it always does. I find I like being the only one who sees it do so, most nights.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Underground we clean the cap lamp glass by feel too. Old men here say you never put your lamp down facing the wall. Don't know why. Never asked. Keep your panes clean.

units.title: Depot at four
units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: four o'clock at the depot and all the buses are lined up in rows with their noses to the wall like horses in a stable and I do the floors of the first six and the windows of the rest and the only noise is the heaters ticking and the night foreman's radio playing old songs and I wouldn't swap it for anything most nights love

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: update: night eight, 03:17, it rang, I said 'goodnight, number', it was silent for forty seconds and hung up. lamp_and_lens I love 'a machine with good manners'. I've put in a ticket asking IT to trace it. team lead says if it's a machine it'll be on an outbound list somewhere and someone forgot to take us off it. that's very boring and I hope it's true

units.title: Three mileposts (a story I'll laugh about by breakfast)
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Breaker breaker. Long empty stretch west of the grain towns, 02:10 local, no moon. Somebody walking the shoulder just past the edge of my headlights, right side. I slowed. They stayed just beyond the lit bit. Milepost 212, 213, 214. Then I hit the next town's lights and the shoulder was empty. Now, I'd done eleven hours. That's highway hypnosis, folks, textbook. Pulled over, had a coffee, stretched. Telling you so you do the same.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Merle, that's the road into my town, you know there's nobody out there on foot at two, the nearest house is eight miles. Which means it was your eyes, which means you need to sleep, which means you're having that coffee at the kennel on Thursday and then a nap in the cab before you go on. Dogs' orders.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Ten-four, Jo. Nap in the cab. I'm laughing about it already, look: big tough trucker, thirty years on the road, scared of a fence post with good timing. There's a cattle grid at 213 with a reflector on a pole, that's probably my walker. Coffee's on me Thursday.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: facilities replied: 'technician scheduled to inspect corridor sensor array'. array! it's six sensors and a light. anyway, they came on again at 01:50, same thing, panel by panel to the last one before the door, then nothing. i did not look up from chapter three. growth. also taro the egg man has been seen buying flour now

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: follow up for anyone who asked, slept twelve hours, oiled the door, it squeaks less. told the lads at the rank and three of them had runners last month, one of them did exactly the stop at the lit car park trick. so probably a runner. I keep telling myself that. anyway back on tonight, short shift, home by four

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: merle mate same week as my runner. we're both getting old. cattle grid reflector is a good one, my version is a bin bag on a bollard that gets me every single time on the bridge road. sleep, coffee, stretch, repeat

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Sorry all, that was rude, leaving mid-sentence. Camera 6, the one on the pole by the trolley bays, suddenly tipped so all I could see was the bottom of its own pole and a puddle. Thought someone was messing with it. Walked over with the big torch: mount bolt had sheared in the gusts and the head had flopped. Nobody about, just a trolley rolling round in the wind. Control made me do a two-page incident form for one bolt. Then my phone died. Lorna, I'm fine, thank you.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Two pages for a bolt is light. Our form for a camera fault is four, plus a photo of the fault, which in your case would have been a puddle. Logged and understood. Glad it was the bolt.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping, gently: Dev, next time a camera does something, finish the sentence with 'brb' so Lorna doesn't have to stay up worrying. Everyone else, thank you for checking on him rather than writing the ending yourselves. That's what this place is for. Ines

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: told you it'd be something boring. not a fox, a bolt, which is a fox for cameras. B corridor lift still sounds like a goose by the way, nobody's filled in a form for that one. I might have to do it myself

units.title: Have you noticed the pattern yet...
units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Read the threads this week. A van that never opens. A figure at the edge of a lot. Lights that walk to a door and stop. A fare who gets out at the edge of a car park. All edges... I won't say what I know about who's buying land in the north, but it's connected, and they're coming. The people in charge already know. You'll see.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: I've removed the opening post and closed this thread. Stitching other members' nights together into a prophecy, with 'they're coming' on the end, is not company on the night shift. Several of the stories you listed have ordinary explanations already posted by the people who lived them. Hollow, you're welcome to tell us about your own night. Ines

units.title: Vending machine report, B corridor
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Weekly report from the B corridor vending machine. Status: still eats every second coin. New stock: a cereal bar that claims to be 'artisan', which it is not. Crisps: the cheese ones are back, morale up. Coffee: brown. The night sister has stuck a note on the front that says 'please be patient with me, I'm old'. Machine of the year.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Our ward machine gives you two of whatever you choose about one time in thirty and the whole night shift knows which button. I won't say which on a public forum. The night sister's note is lovely. Solidarity from Halvard. Back to it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I would read a whole novel narrated by that vending machine. Please be patient with me, I'm old: that's the first line, and a good one. I've taken your detective novel advice, incidentally, and I'm on chapter three and suspicious of the vicar already.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Log, 01:05 local. Replacement for camera 14 approved, fitting next week. Figure present on 14 from 00:20 to 00:48, same pixels, as Dmitra said. Patrolled south fence during that window as a check. Nil found. Reefer stack hums, gulls, one fox by the gatehouse. Artefact consistent. Logged.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Van report: there again last night, and tonight. I went out with the bins at four and tried for the plate, still muck. I left a warm roll on the bonnet in a paper bag, which is either kind or deranged. By five the roll was gone. The van was still there, engine running. Somebody in there likes caraway, apparently.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: The roll gone and the engine running sounds like a sleepy driver with good taste. I'll come in for my loaf at six and look at it myself on the way past, and if it's still there I'll knock on the window. Pharmacists are used to waking people up. Ines
